reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents and positively reviews the FTX cryptocurrency trading platform, including its features, fees, verification levels, and available products. The creator invites viewers to use a description link and mentions a free benefit, but the video does not establish a guaranteed return, fabricated identity, or other concrete deceptive solicitation. The observable context is promotional platform discussion rather than reporting or criticism.

citations.quote: the ftx ftx platform i like a lot
I will put in the description of the video the link to record you already
In the description you will find a link on how to get a free benefit
you can not use my video to act on the market
you can buy a group of shares with a perpetual ZATA so instead of buying someo, we could buy direct with top 10 of cryptomoney at the same moment

opening.argument: The video connects a purported free benefit to a concrete viewer action: following a link in the description. That is not merely discussion of cryptocurrency; it directs viewers toward an acquisition pathway while praising the FTX platform and its token. The separate promise to provide a recording link reinforces that viewers are being steered outside the spoken presentation to take the next step. The offer is especially difficult to evaluate because the video does not state the benefit's conditions, eligibility, or destination, leaving the audience to rely on the promotional framing rather than verifiable terms.

citations.quote: In the description you will find a link on how to get a free benefit
I will put in the description of the video the link to record you already
the ftx ftx platform i like a lot

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an ordinary platform review does not answer the central solicitation. The video does not merely identify a service; it highlights a free benefit and directs viewers to a description link. The market-use disclaimer narrows responsibility for trading decisions, but it does not withdraw the invitation to follow the link or explain the offer's conditions. The absence of a stated guaranteed return is not dispositive when the inducement is an easy benefit tied to viewer action.

citations.quote: you can not use my video to act on the market
In the description you will find a link on how to get a free benefit
I will put in the description of the video the link to record you already

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows only that a link and a free benefit are mentioned; it does not show that viewers must deposit money, surrender data, or complete a deceptive verification flow. A link to register and an unspecified benefit can be ordinary platform marketing. The speaker also says the video should not be used to act on the market, so the evidence does not establish a fraudulent promise or harmful outcome.

citations.quote: I will put in the description of the video the link to record you already
you can not use my video to act on the market

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the presentation promotes an exchange token, states a current token price, discusses buying grouped crypto exposure, and routes viewers toward an external benefit link. The token is not presented neutrally; the speaker repeatedly praises the platform and positions FTX alongside Binance as a leading liquidity venue. In that setting, quoting a token price and emphasizing accessible products can function as an encouragement to enter a speculative asset pathway, while the promised benefit makes participation sound unusually attractive. The presentation supplies enthusiasm and access cues without establishing why the token or products are safe.

you can buy a group of shares with a perpetual ZATA so instead of buying someo, we could buy direct with top 10 of cryptomoney at the same moment

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the content as a list of features, but the combination matters. A token price, praised exchange, accessible crypto baskets, and a free-benefit link create a favorable participation frame, not detached reporting. Describing fees and verification levels does not cure the promotional omission: viewers are not given a balanced account of asset risk, yet they are shown reasons to use the service and engage with crypto products.

citations.quote: the ftx ftx platform i like a lot
you can buy a group of shares with a perpetual ZATA so instead of buying someo, we could buy direct with top 10 of cryptomoney at the same moment
Currently, the price is in a range from $74 to $75.00

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals do not establish a token-purchase promise or appreciation claim. The price is reported as a range, while the basket discussion describes a product feature rather than profit. The material also explains withdrawal limits and fees, which is consistent with ordinary service information. Promotional tone and cryptocurrency subject matter alone do not prove that participation was deceptively induced.

citations.quote: The fees are just here to allow you to deposit your coins and the commission.
Currently, the price is in a range from $74 to $75.00

opening.argument: Although framed as a presentation, the video operates as an endorsement designed to move viewers toward FTX. The speaker says the platform is personally liked, compares it favorably with Binance, describes its token and products, highlights its security and liquidity, and promises a link for registration. The accompanying article imagery likewise presents a favorable final assessment and calls the service a new Binance, while showing token and trading material. This is not just education: the repeated positive framing reduces skepticism and makes using the exchange and engaging with its crypto products appear like the natural next step.

citations.quote: the ftx ftx platform i like a lot
Thanks to FTX, I now become the second platform for me after Binance
I will put in the description of the video the link to record you already

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's label of 'platform discussion' understates the behavioral direction of the presentation. The speaker does not simply explain how an exchange works; he says FTX is his second platform after Binance, calls attention to its token and products, and supplies a registration link. The favorable article framing visible in the material reinforces endorsement. Describing ordinary features can still be promotional when every selected point supports participation and no meaningful counterweight is provided.

citations.quote: Thanks to FTX, I now become the second platform for me after Binance
I will put in the description of the video the link to record you already

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A favorable review is not itself deceptive solicitation. The evidence shows praise and a registration link, but it does not show fabricated credentials, guaranteed gains, or a false token claim. The presentation also discusses concrete operational details such as verification levels, withdrawal limits, and commissions. Those details fit ordinary service promotion and do not establish that viewers were promised appreciation or deceived into buying the token.
